title: Distributor registration, AMFI code of conduct and ethics
objectives: Explain ARN, EUIN and the NISM requirement.
Apply the AMFI code of conduct.
body_md:
## Becoming a distributor

- Pass **NISM-Series-V-A** and register with **AMFI** to get an **ARN** (AMFI Registration Number).
- Each employee or sub-broker who sells uses an **EUIN** (Employee Unique Identification Number) to trace the advice.
- Certification and ARN must be **renewed**.

## What a distributor may and may not do

| Allowed | Not allowed |
|---|---|
| Sell and service MF products | Handle client money (cheques go to the AMC) |
| Give **incidental advice** on products | Give personalised portfolio advice for a fee without IA registration |
| Earn commission disclosed to clients | Promise returns |
| Provide statements and service | Churn clients for commission |

## AMFI code of conduct (principles)

- Act in the client's interest; know the product and the client.
- Disclose all commission and conflicts; give the **correct risk disclosure**.
- Use only **approved** and accurate marketing material.
- Maintain confidentiality; refer complaints on time.
- Never mis-sell, rebate against the rules, or spread rumours.

> **Exam tip:** ARN for the firm, EUIN for the person.
example: A distributor moves a client from one fund to another to earn a higher commission without a client reason. That is churning and breaches the code.
say: I earn a trail commission from the AMC; Direct plans cost less.
Please write cheques to the fund, not to me.
never: Give me a cheque in my name and I will invest it for you.
This fund will give 18% every year.

check.why: EUIN identifies the individual who sold the product.

check.q: A distributor should take cheques made out to:
check.why: Cheques go to the scheme; distributors never handle client money.

check.q: Switching a client purely to earn a higher commission is:
check.why: Churning is trading in the distributor's interest, not the client's.
